FINAL FOR IMPLEMENTATION — Status board, dark by default (15 Sep 2026).

This page is the reference for plan 012. The tokens, type ramp and component rules are written out in docs/design-brief.md → Design guidelines; the artboards here are the picture of them.

Charcoal ground, warm off-white type, hairline panels, a real table on desktop that folds into stacked rows on the phone. Status is always a glyph + word chip; anything wrong tints its row. Numbers are monospace so columns align.

Dark is served to everyone by default; the warm-paper light scheme (the Dark switch) is the explicit alternative.

Calendar sources use blue, amber and violet — chosen so they stay distinct for colour-blind readers.

Type: IBM Plex Sans (@fontsource-variable/ibm-plex-sans) + IBM Plex Mono (@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono).

The three directions not chosen, kept for reference.

Every frame shows the same household as the Status board page: 8 probes (1 down, 1 unstable, 1 paused), 2 backups (1 late), 5 links, weather, and a 4-day calendar with 3 sources. Names are placeholders. Each artboard has a Dark switch.

A · Tinted tiles

Closest to the reference screenshots: a deep blue-slate ground, lighter tinted tiles, icon + name + detail, a haloed dot with the status word on the right and the uptime under it.

Tradeoff: colour on colour — orange and red fight the blue ground.

Type: Manrope.

C · Warm home

The family-first read: a sentence headline, big rounded cards with a 48px status glyph, weather and calendar as first-class panels. Cream ground, terracotta accent.

Tradeoff: generated headline copy must stay honest for forty probes and for zero; lowest card density.

Type: DM Sans.

D · Dark console

Colour as signal only: near-black, one desaturated accent, status hues are the only chroma. Square LED + uppercase state word, uptime as the hero numeral.

Tradeoff: the most technical tone; the light variant reads as a plain grey utility.

Type: Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono.
